global_read: state/global.json (fetched 2026-09-01 08:46) confirms this checkpoint's trigger is real, not stale news: Brent 92.15 (+1.83% 1d, +10.0% 1mo) and WTI 87.50 (+2.03% 1d, +8.91% 1mo) are both up sharply after the US struck Iranian positions on Larak Island and Iran retaliated against US-linked bases in Jordan -- a genuine energy-price shock, confirmed independently this run via CNBC/Washington Post reporting. VIX 15.55 (+4.22% 1d) and a soft S&P (-0.58% 1d) / Dow (-0.72% 1d) show global risk appetite turning cautious in sympathy, though VIX's absolute level is still low, not a panic reading. Gold +9.66% 1mo keeps a safe-haven premium bid. USD/PKR (277.29) and DXY (99.62) are both essentially flat -- the FX channel has not cracked yet, a genuine near-term positive, but oil is Pakistan's direct transmission channel (petroleum was FY26's single largest import category) regardless of what the rupee does today. Net: global tape has flipped from last week's calm-to-constructive read to a mild-but-real risk-off tilt, driven specifically by the same conflict this checkpoint is escalating on.
drivers: US forces struck two Iranian rocket-launcher positions on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on 2026-08-30/31 (first acknowledged combat since late July); Iran's IRGC confirmed casualties and retaliated by targeting US military installations in Jordan; Brent jumped as much as 3.4% intraday to $91.09/bbl, WTI to $86.22/bbl -- re-verified this run via https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/08/30/us-strikes-iran-missile-sites-larak-island/ and https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/31/oil-prices-hormuz-iran-larak-island-centcom.html

PSX's confirmed 2026-08-31 close: KSE-100 down 720.83pts (-0.41%) to 176,975.68 on the escalation and higher oil, with broad selling across autos, cement, banks, OMCs, E&P and power -- refineries (PRL/NRL/ATRL) were the lone outperforming sector on higher crack-spread expectations, a nuance against a blanket 'oil is bad for everything' read -- re-verified this run via https://www.brecorder.com/news/40437196/psx-kse-100-index-falls-721-points-amid-us-iran-conflict

Transmission to Pakistan is real but partly lagged: petroleum was FY26's largest single import category at $16.86bn (+5.76% YoY) of a $69.76bn total import bill, so a sustained Brent move near/above $90 widens the import bill and pressures the current account and reserves the July print (a genuine positive) does not yet capture. At the pump the pass-through is muted for now -- Pakistan moved to a near-daily OGRA fuel-price review mechanism after 2026's Middle East volatility, and the 2026-09-01 revision (using a 7-day rolling average) lifted petrol only 77 paisa to Rs342.79/litre while diesel actually fell -- re-verified this run via https://mashriqtv.pk/en/petrol-price-in-pakistan-today/ ; a full pass-through will show up in the rolling average only if Brent holds at these levels.

SBP-held FX reserves last printed $17,098.5mn (~$17.10bn) for the week ended 2026-08-21 (+$17mn WoW), total liquid reserves ~$22.6bn -- no fresher weekly print exists yet this checkpoint, re-verified this run via https://www.brecorder.com/news/40435778/sbp-held-forex-reserves-rise-by-25mn-to-1708bn ; a reserve buffer this thin (~2.6 months import cover) has little room to absorb a sustained oil-driven import-bill increase without PKR or reserve stress.

SBP held the policy rate at 11.5% at its last MPC (2026-07-27); next decision 2026-09-14. July CPI was 9.2% YoY; the August print was due '~2026-09-01' but has NOT yet been released as of this checkpoint (re-checked this run via PBS and search) -- independent forecasts (AKD 11.4%, Topline 10.75-11.25%) already pointed to a reversal back into double digits before this oil shock; the shock is a fresh upside risk to that print and to the Sept 14 rate decision, not a reason to expect an early cut -- source https://www.pbs.gov.pk/price-statistics/

IMF's 4th EFF / 3rd RSF review mission is now reported expected to arrive in the second week of September 2026 (schedule not yet finalized); Pakistan is reported on track to meet 6 of 7 quantitative performance criteria ahead of the review, with ~$1.2bn combined disbursement (~$1bn EFF + ~$200mn RSF) at stake; energy-sector circular debt remains the key unresolved sticking point -- re-verified this run via https://www.techjuice.pk/pakistan-likely-to-meet-six-of-seven-imf-targets-ahead-of-september-review/ and https://dailytimes.com.pk/1545032/imf-mission-expected-in-pakistan-next-month-for-loan-programme-reviews/

PKR has held remarkably flat at ~277.60/USD interbank for 12 straight sessions through end-August into 2026-09-01 despite the oil shock -- a genuine short-term positive that the FX channel hasn't cracked, though it leaves the rupee with less of a demonstrated cushion if the conflict widens further -- re-verified this run via https://arynews.tv/pkr-us-dollar-rate-august-end-saudi-riyal-uae-dirham-flat

Desk geo-risk radar (state/georisk.json, 2026-09-01 08:46) reads 62/100 'moderate', up from 54 three sessions ago: conflict/escalation stress pinned at the 100 max, and energy-shock stress jumped from 47 to 75 this run on the Brent move -- this checkpoint's own escalation trigger is now directly visible in the radar, not just in news headlines. Band stays 'moderate' rather than crossing into an explicit 'elevated/high' label, but the direction of travel plus the severity-5 trigger argue for treating this cycle defensively rather than waiting for the band label itself to flip.

favored: refineries (ATRL/NRL/PRL) -- the one sector that actually outperformed on the 2026-08-31 sell-off, benefiting from higher crack-spread expectations at elevated crude, plus the pending $6bn refinery-upgrade policy tailwind; a narrower, more defensible expression of the oil move than E&P/OMC broadly

large, well-capitalized banks holding government paper -- the T-bill/PIB carry tailwind (6M 11.80%, 10Y PIB 12.30%) persists into the Sept 14 MPC and is a genuine quality/defensive anchor in a risk-off tape, distinct from small/thinly-capitalized names
avoid: OMCs -- squeezed between a volatile, near-daily-reset pump price and rising import cost of the product itself; sold off alongside the broader market on 2026-08-31 despite the crude move, unlike refiners

autos, cement and power/IPPs -- all named among the broad-based sellers on 2026-08-31; power/IPPs carry the added overhang of the unresolved circular-debt sticking point heading into the IMF's September review

small/thinly-capitalized banks and rate-sensitive high-leverage names -- the pending August CPI print (independently forecast 10.75-11.4% YoY even before this oil shock) and elevated, still-rising T-bill/PIB cutoffs argue against pricing in near-term rate relief

broad cyclicals / index-chasing -- geo-risk radar is 62/100 'moderate' and rising (energy-shock stress 47->75 this run), the conflict is in its sixth month and actively escalating (fresh strikes and retaliation this cycle), and gold's persistent safe-haven bid (+9.66% 1mo) signals global sentiment remains defensive; this is not a tape to add broad risk into
